Figure 1: Headline key-side payoff on the damage-bearing 2-bit key-only rows. The main-text HeadQ setting lowers ∆PPL relative to the KIVI-like baseline across the main affected models; lower is better.
Table 2: K-side counterexample to raw key MSE. Lower key MSE does not imply lower KL or output error. Bold marks the better value within each model/metric comparison.
Figure 2: Matched low-entropy Pythia probes. The 160M anomaly is tied to an exact route-flip regime; the boundary weakens sharply by 410M and 1B within the same family.

Figure 4: Full-KV quantizer-corrector codec composition on the damage-bearing 2-bit rows; lower is better. The key-side HeadQ correction composes with the A2-guided value policy and improves all six models. Appendix Table 7 retains the broader KV-bit frontier.

Table 4: Full causal null-space control at α = 1. Restoring a softmax-null mean-key component increases damage for fixed-grid block and group absmax-4 K quantizers, while per-channel affine K remains translation-equivariant. Values near zero indicate no inert-mean penalty.

Table 5: Appendix key-only HeadQ rank/bit frontier. Entries are percent PPL deltas versus dense on four WikiText-103 windows at length 128 with prefill 64. The main text uses the rank-4 setting; rank-2 and other bit widths are retained here for completeness.

Table 3: Deployable query-PCA approximation from the six-model, 12- calibration-prompt sweep. Learned score-visible bases recover most of the diagnostic oracle benefit, while equal-overhead random bases do not.

Table 7: Appendix full-KV codec bit frontier. Entries are percent PPL deltas versus dense on four WikiText-103 windows at length 128 with prefill 64. The main text emphasizes the 2-bit rows; broader KV-bit variants are retained here for completeness.
